## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kharādiyajātaka* (Ja 15), titled *With Kharādiya* in English, is a canonical birth-story preserved in the Pali *Jātaka* collection. In the narrative framework recorded in the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the Buddha delivers the story while residing at Jetavana with reference to an unruly monk (*dubbacabhikkhu*) who refused to heed admonition (*ovādam na gaṇhati*) [Fausböll 1877]. The Buddha relates that in a past life, this same individual also suffered misfortune on account of disobedience, opening the verse with the line *Aṭṭhakhuraṁ Kharādiye* ("For when a deer...") [Fausböll 1877]. In modern studies, Diana Y. Paul notes the *Kharādiyajātaka* in her discussion of female characters in the Jātakas associated with Mahāpajāpatī [Paul 1985].
